scope: P8/R04 functional two-port transport scheduling increment; R05/P9 timing/resource and Q14 qualification remain open.

architecture.tasks: Existing one control task; unchanged WAMR workers and priorities
architecture.ports: Distinct management/application sockets; authority and collector management-only
round: Application TX up to endpoint reservation cap
Management replies and complete finite peer pass
At most one eligible artifact attempt
architecture.pacing_semantics: Attempt spacing persists across blocks/retries/failure/restart/new transfer; zero disables. Terminal timeout bypasses pacing; no deadline renewal.
architecture.lifecycle: Due timers before each receive and application send; accepted input has pre/post lifecycle decisions under registry lock.
architecture.continuation: Exhausted receive/transmit budget gives deadline 0; run repeats without another external wake.
architecture.fairness: Existing persistent endpoint cursor by message; full management peer pass needs no extra cursor.
architecture.application_semantics: Best effort, dequeue before send, failure does not requeue.
architecture.relay: One policy/RNG per directed link across both classes; one global pending-copy heap/capacity; reverse link independent.

reviews.scheduler: Independent review found no protocol blocker; retained full finite peer pass as simplest fairness design.
reviews.embedded_stack: Removed duplicate reply datagram temporary/copy; receive handlers encode into existing bounded reply storage.
reviews.fixture_regression: Preserved behavioral assertions; excessive unconditional lifecycle passes discovered by an existing worker-entry assertion were corrected using due-timer checks between empty phases.

limitations: Two sockets do not reserve radio airtime or fully isolate lower network buffers.
Management and artifact responses share the management receive FIFO.
Receive fairness is by class, not endpoint; noisy application producer can fill the shared application socket.
Continuous host work can keep ESP priority-3 control runnable ahead of priority-2 workers on the same core.
No declared workload rates/latency/loss/progress acceptance limits; short POSIX runs do not qualify them.
No physical Wi-Fi/heap/stack measurements, complete lock-wait/hold instrumentation or timer-lateness measurement.
No separated RX-to-enqueue, Put-to-submission or guest-consumption/acquisition-age timing guarantee.
Kernel socket loss and observer overhead not isolated; successful send is not remote receipt.
Q14 final composed scheduler model and R05/P9 qualification remain open.
